title: Navigating the Editor 🖱️
description: Learn to fly through your 3D world like a pro.

slides.title: The Interface at a Glance 👀
slides.content:
# Meet the Editor

When your project opens, you’ll see several panels:

* **Viewport** – your 3D window into the world
* **Content Browser** – file manager for assets
* **World Outliner** – list of all actors in the level
* **Details Panel** – properties of selected object
* **Modes Panel** – tools for placing objects (landscape, painting, etc.)

*Analogy:* Think of the editor like a **cockpit** – each panel gives you control over a different part of your world.

quizData.question: Which panel shows all the objects currently in your level?
quizData.explanation: The World Outliner lists every actor placed in your level. The Content Browser shows asset files.

slides.title: Viewport Controls 🕹️
slides.content:
## How to Move in 3D

* **Right Mouse Button (hold)** – look around (fly mode)
* **WASD** (while holding right mouse) – fly forward/back/left/right
* **Q / E** – fly down / up
* **Mouse Scroll Wheel** – zoom in/out
* **Scroll Click + Drag** – pan the view
* **F** (with object selected) – focus camera on object

Try it: hold **Right Mouse** and press **W** to fly forward! 🦅

quizData.question: Which key do you press to fly upward while holding right mouse button?
quizData.explanation: Holding right mouse and pressing E flies the camera up; Q flies down.

slides.title: Customizing Your Layout 🎨
slides.content:
## Make It Yours

You can drag panels around, resize, or create **new tabs**. Common presets:

* **Default** – standard arrangement
* **UE4 Classic** – old‑school layout (tighter)
* **Cinematic** – larger viewport for film work

Switch via **Window** → **Load Layout** → choose one. For now, stick with Default.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Quick Focus

Lost in space? Select any object in the World Outliner and press **F** – the camera will snap to it. Great for finding your way around!
